/// An expectation on a value, from `that` on an `Expect`. Each method asserts
/// how the value compares to the expected one and records a failure on the test
/// when it does not hold.
export class Expectation<T> {
    /// An expectation that negates the assertion that follows.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(5).never.is(3);
    /// expect.that(5).never.greaterThan(10);
    /// ```
    get never(): Expectation<T>;

    /// Asserts that the value equals the expected value. Class instances
    /// compare by reference unless their class overloads `==`.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(5).is(5);
    /// expect.that("hello").is("hello");
    /// ```
    is(expected: T): void;

    /// Asserts that the value is less than the expected value.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(3).lessThan(10);
    /// ```
    lessThan(expected: T): void;

    /// Asserts that the value is less than or equal to the expected value.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(5).lessThanOrEqual(5);
    /// expect.that(4).lessThanOrEqual(5);
    /// ```
    lessThanOrEqual(expected: T): void;

    /// Asserts that the value is greater than the expected value.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(10).greaterThan(5);
    /// ```
    greaterThan(expected: T): void;

    /// Asserts that the value is greater than or equal to the expected value.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(5).greaterThanOrEqual(5);
    /// expect.that(6).greaterThanOrEqual(5);
    /// ```
    greaterThanOrEqual(expected: T): void;
}

/// Creates expectations for one test case. Each test body receives its own
/// `Expect`, and a helper that asserts takes it as a parameter.
export class Expect {
    /// Starts an `Expectation` on `value`. A failure reports `line`, which
    /// defaults to the line of the call.
    /// ```as
    /// expect.that(2 + 3).is(5);
    /// ```
    that<T>(value: T, line: i32 = callerLine()): Expectation<T>;
}

/// A test suite. Extend it, export the class, and declare test cases and groups
/// in `run`. The editor's test pane and `rive <dir> --test` run every exported
/// suite.
///
/// Test code exists only at edit time and never ships in the exported file.
/// Subclasses of `Tests` are edit time already; mark any other declaration
/// that names `Expect` or `Expectation`, such as a helper, `@editTime`.
/// ```as
/// import { Expect, Tests } from "rive/test";
///
/// function clamp(value: f64, low: f64, high: f64): f64 {
///   return Math.min(Math.max(value, low), high);
/// }
///
/// @editTime
/// function expectClamped(expect: Expect, value: f64, want: f64): void {
///   expect.that(clamp(value, 0, 5)).is(want);
/// }
///
/// export class MathTests extends Tests {
///   override run(): void {
///     group("clamp", () => {
///       test("clamps high values", (expect) => {
///         expectClamped(expect, 10, 5);
///       });
///       test("passes values in range through", (expect) => {
///         expect.that(clamp(3, 0, 5)).is(3);
///       });
///     });
///   }
/// }
/// ```
export abstract class Tests extends Protocol {
    /// Declares the suite's test cases and groups by calling `test` and
    /// `group`. Inside `run` and its lambdas they need no `this.`.
    abstract run(): void;

    /// Looks up a blob asset by name, or null when it is missing or empty.
    /// The test runner supplies the project's blobs.
    /// ```as
    /// test("reads fixtures", (expect) => {
    ///     let data = this.blob("fixtures");
    ///     expect.that(data != null).is(true);
    /// });
    /// ```
    unsafe blob(name: string): ArrayBuffer?;

    /// Groups related test cases under a common name. Groups can nest.
    /// ```as
    /// group("math", () => {
    ///   test("adds numbers", (expect) => {
    ///     expect.that(2 + 2).is(4);
    ///   });
    ///   test("multiplies numbers", (expect) => {
    ///     expect.that(3 * 4).is(12);
    ///   });
    /// });
    /// ```
    group(name: string, body: () => void): void;

    /// Declares a named test case. `body` receives the case's `Expect`, used to
    /// create expectations on values.
    /// ```as
    /// test("adds two numbers", (expect) => {
    ///   let result = 2 + 3;
    ///   expect.that(result).is(5);
    /// });
    /// ```
    test(name: string, body: (expect: Expect) => void): void;

    /// Declares a test case that passes only when `body` throws. With a
    /// `message`, the error must also contain it. A case that runs past its
    /// time budget fails.
    /// ```as
    /// errors("rejects a negative size", (expect) => {
    ///   Buffer.create(-1);
    /// }, "invalid argument #1 to 'create' (size)");
    /// ```
    errors(
        name: string,
        body: (expect: Expect) => void,
        message: string = ""
    ): void;
}
